text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Helsinki region now has 900,000 inhabitants after an increase of 15,000 last year, with particularly active migration from smaller cities and municipalities nearby.

- Finland becomes championship favourite for the Ice Hockey World Championships it hosts in April after winning the European title through 4-2 victory over arch rival Sweden 4-2 in final of four-country tournament in Stockholm. @

- Paper worker strike at Kerta Oy in Kotka may expand to the whole of south-eastern Finland unless a settlement is reached in a dispute on whether the national pay deal applies to Kerta's paper workers, says union chairman Jarmo Lahteenmaki.
- Large supermarkets do not always increase private traffic, study shows.
- The public sector would lose billions of markka if they stopped subsidising mass transport, traffic ministry report says. @
- Local cooperative banks distancing themselves from the banking bloc integrating around OKOBANK -- may become a totally separate banking group.
- Kone's loss-making Italian unit should return to the black this year, putting the total amount of losses at 250 million markka, says managing director Anssi Soila.
- Foreign financial services companies have visited virtually all Finnish financial firms to find partners, says Pasi Vare, managing director at state-owned Postipankki's PSP-Rahoitus. @
- Moral hazard was a more important factor in Finland's savings bank crisis in the early 1990s than earlier believed, study shows.

- National pension fund Kela, with a 2.7 billion markka share portfolio plus a 4.4 percent stake in state-owned power producer Imatran Voima, has restricted trading policy but director Antti Arola says it could arguably become somewhat more active. @
- MEP Esko Seppanen says Finland's leaders will start leading Finland towards NATO membership as soon as Finland has joined Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
- MEP Pertti Paasio says the EU should be able to use union resources in serious unemployment situations.
